lessons.title: Lesson 1: Hello World & Variables
lessons.html:
Your First Rust Program

Rust is a systems programming language that guarantees memory safety without garbage collection.

Basic Structure:

  • fn main() - Every Rust program starts here
  • println!() - Macro to print formatted text
  • ; - Required at end of statements
fn main() {
    println!("Hello, Rust!");
    let x = 5;
    let name = "Alice";
    println!("x = {}, name = {}", x, name);
}

Key Concept: Variables are immutable by default. Add mut to make mutable: let mut x = 5;

lessons.title: Lesson 2: Data Types & Operators
lessons.html:
Primitive Data Types

Rust has type inference but strict typing. Compiler usually guesses the type correctly.

Main Types:

TypeExampleDescription
i3242Signed 32-bit integer
u3242u32Unsigned 32-bit integer
f643.1464-bit float (default)
booltrueBoolean
fn main() {
    let guess: u32 = "42".parse().expect("Not a number!");
    let x = 2.0;  // f64
    let y: f32 = 3.0;  // 32-bit float
    let sum = 5 + 10;
    let logical = true && false;
    println!("Results: {}, {}, {}", guess, sum, logical);
}

lessons.title: Lesson 3: Functions & Control Flow
lessons.html:
Functions and Control Structures

Functions are declared with fn. Last expression (without ;) becomes return value.

Function Example:

fn add(a: i32, b: i32) -> i32 {
    a + b  // No semicolon = return value
}

Control Flow:

  • if/else: Expressions that return values
  • loop: Infinite loop with break
  • while: Loop while condition is true
fn main() {
    let result = add(5, 3);
    let number = 6;
    let is_divisible = if number % 4 == 0 {
        println!("divisible");
        true
    } else {
        println!("not divisible");
        false
    };
}

lessons.title: Lesson 4: Ownership Basics
lessons.html:
Rust's Ownership Model

Rust ensures memory safety through ownership. No garbage collector needed!

Three Rules:

  1. Each value has a single variable (owner)
  2. Only one owner at a time
  3. When owner goes out of scope, value is dropped
fn main() {
    let s = String::from("hello");  // s owns the value
    // takes_ownership(s);  // Error! s moved into function
    
    let x = 5;
    makes_copy(x);  // i32 implements Copy trait
    println!("x = {}", x);  // Still works!
}

Copy Types: Simple types like i32, bool can be copied freely.

lessons.title: Lesson 5: Structs & Enums
lessons.html:
Custom Data Types

Structs combine multiple related values. Enums represent different variants of data.

Struct Example:

struct Person {
    name: String,
    age: u8,
}
fn main() {
    let p = Person {
        name: String::from("Bob"),
        age: 30,
    };
    println!("{} is {} years old", p.name, p.age);
}

Enum Example:

enum Message {
    Quit,
    Move { x: i32, y: i32 },
    Write(String),
    ChangeColor(i32, i32, i32),
}
